title: A map from a finite to a finitely presented module that is bijective at a prime is bijective after inverting one element
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal, $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $N$ a finitely presented $A$-module (there is an exact sequence $A^{\oplus u}\to A^{\oplus v}\to N\to0$ for some $u,v\ge0$) and $\varphi:M\to N$ an $A$-linear map. Suppose that the localized map $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}:M_{\mathfrak p}\to N_{\mathfrak p}$, $m/s\mapsto\varphi(m)/s$, between the localizations at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], is bijective. Then there is $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that the localized map $\varphi_g:M_g\to N_g$, $m/g^k\mapsto\varphi(m)/g^k$, between the localizations at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], is bijective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GF (lemma-map-between-finitely-presented: the set of primes q with phi_q an isomorphism is open in Spec A) combined with Lemma Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local: a module whose localizations at all primes vanish is zero), exactly as the two are combined in the proof of Lemma Tag 0GWM (lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free)
